The Hunnish Kings.
When this means was revealed {OCR?},
he sent and said:
"There is no need for troops;
do not send anyone,"
while removing from him any evil suspicion.
Baidu, however, relaxed a little,
and he used to see a shadow as a body,
and by the tricks, devices, and crafts of these men he was beguiled like a babe.
And he drove away from around him contention, war, and battles,
and began to indulge himself in eating and drinking only.
However, by lascivious lust he was not overcome at all,
nor was his mind captivated by a strange woman apart from his wives,
nor was he pleased to behave dissolutely in a Sodomite manner like him who was before him, that is, Gaikhatu (p. 258).
Rather, he conducted himself with intelligence, orderliness, and a praiseworthy humility of mind;
and the virtuous, wise, chaste, and ascetics who were present from whatever nation it might be, he used to receive and honour,
and enrich with gifts,
and adorn with royal garments.
And because for a long period of years he had conversed with Despina, the daughter of the king of the Greeks, who was the wife of Abaqa {OCR?},
his intention inclined towards the side of the Christians,
and for some years he used to take a church and a clapper around in his camp;
yet to be openly named a Christian, he was ashamed.
And because at this time {OCR?} all the Mongols, great and small, had in their entirety become Muslims,
and had already been circumcised,
and had become very skilled {OCR?} in the ablutions and prayers which are peculiar to the Muslims,
Baidu also, wishing to please them, became a Muslim,
and all the nobles of his kingdom rejoiced in him very greatly.
Yet he was not able to restrain himself from the company of Christians,
and he could not bring himself to trust any human being in all the administrations of the kingdom apart from them.
And from here {OCR?} he began to halt between both sides.
To the Christians, indeed, he used to say {OCR?} that he was a Christian,
and a cross hung on his neck.
To the Arabs, however, he used to show {OCR?} that he was a Muslim,
saying, "I am not able to learn the ablutions and fasts."
And whenever the heads of their religion were present with him and stood up for prayer,
that Baidu used to send his son to pray with them.
